dedupe_keys.name: spain 28 april 2025 blackout impact on emergency medical services

description: This case study analyses how the blackout of 28 April 2025, which cut power to mainland Spain and Portugal for over ten hours, affected emergency medical services in Spain. The authors, emergency physicians and researchers from the University of Oviedo, the Health Service of Asturias (SAMU-Asturias), the RINVEMER prehospital research network of the Spanish Society of Emergency Medicine and other services, wrote an urgent analysis published in 2025 in Prehospital and Disaster Medicine, free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is national, drawing on regional services. Caveats: this is a rapid expert analysis, not a systematic data study, and the cause of the blackout was still uncertain. The authors report that no region had a specific contingency plan for power outages; traffic signal failures caused accidents and delayed response; the collapse of communication networks affected 1-1-2 emergency calls; fuel shortages arose as petrol stations stopped; and patients using home medical devices were endangered, with at least one death from ventilator failure. Many services lacked backup communications, such as satellite phones or analogue radios, and many hospitals and ambulance bases lacked stable generators and fuel; coordination suffered from incompatible protocols, although services adapted by prioritising urgent care. Simulation uses: a failure chain linking power loss to emergency service performance for cascading failure and preparedness models. Related records: the Texas 2021 winter storm blackout (case_study-texas-february-2021-winter-storm-blackout) describes another prolonged outage.
